rationale: The target buyers — developers and technical PMs — are a real software-buying cohort (they pay $12–45/mo for Figma), so commercial reality is plausible, but willingness to pay specifically for a text-based wireframing DSL is unproven and niche within that group. Building a credible MermaidJS-style DSL requires a non-trivial parser and renderer that goes beyond Claude prompts plus a simple page — this is genuine software engineering that likely exceeds the factory's current build envelope. Even if shipped, the market is small and several open-source alternatives (Structurizr, Wireframe DSL projects) exist, keeping defensibility low.
solution_plan: WHAT: A hosted service where you describe a UI wireframe in plain text (e.g., 'header with nav, two-column body, sidebar') and Claude renders a shareable PNG or simple HTML wireframe. BUILD: The factory would create a Claude prompt that converts text descriptions to basic HTML/ASCII wireframe output, wrap it in a simple form page, and attach a Stripe payment link for a $9/mo subscription — no coding by the operator, but the render quality will be limited without a real DSL engine. SELL: Reach developers on Twitter/X (using #buildinpublic, #devtools), Product Hunt, and Hacker News 'Ask HN' — the factory drafts outreach copy and posts only after the operator approves. MAINTAIN: Submissions arrive via the form, Claude generates wireframes, results are emailed back; Stripe handles billing automatically, and Claude handles support FAQs — the operator's only recurring task is approving outreach batches. CAUTION: The core output quality is likely to disappoint developers expecting a real DSL; this needs a validation spike (10–20 user tests) before committing to build.
notes: buildability_with_ai is borderline (scored 4); a true MermaidJS-equivalent DSL is not achievable with prompts alone — the factory would deliver a weaker 'describe-and-render' service, which may not satisfy the stated need. Validate first.
